findings.rationale: The status enum generated for every effect declares the members Cancelled and Compensated, but no generated action ever assigns status[correlation] to either member. The only status writes are status=Pending on request trigger and on retry, and status=effect_outcome_member on completion, which yields Succeeded/Failed/TimedOut. Cancelled and Compensated are therefore unreachable dead states, leaving the effect state machine incomplete.

In each command action the guard rejects only correlations whose status is Pending or Succeeded, so a Failed/TimedOut/Cancelled/Compensated effect is re-armed: status is set back to Pending and attempts is reset to 1. Because attempts is reset on every request-event emission instead of being accumulated, the max_attempts cap enforced by the dedicated retry action can be bypassed by re-emitting the request event, permitting unbounded retries.

The attempt counter type is declared 0..max_attempts (defaulting to 0..1 when max_attempts is absent), yet the request trigger writes attempts=1 and the retry action guards on attempts < maximum and then writes attempts = attempts + 1, reaching exactly maximum. Under an exclusive upper bound these writes fall outside the declared range (1 outside 0..1, and maximum outside 0..maximum), so the guard permits a write that violates the counter domain, an off-by-one between the guard/write and the type bound.

event_assignments sets every event flag to false except those in the emitted set, and each effect-completion or saga-observation action emits exactly one event, so event flags are mutually exclusive with at most one true at a time. Saga guards for a step whose awaits_mode is all, however, require multiple awaited event flags to be simultaneously true, so those all-mode steps can never satisfy their guard and are unreachable.
